name: Ren Berry
life: “I still remember tuning an engine in the dark to spare a sleeping crew.” On Monday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Ren knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I tuned that engine solely by ear. I can hear which part was replaced while I was away.
appearance: Ren has a neat white crop, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. When somebody else has the floor, Ren grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Ren prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To identify the change in the engine sound.
family: Allen Mora is Ren’s younger cousin. Ren offers the first invitation. Allen gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The third bedroom*, Allen says, “I do the assessment. I brought a tape measure and ended up drawing two alternate plans on the kitchen floor.”
connections: Sky Avery (parts supplier). A mechanic demonstrates a familiar note to the parts supplier's apprentice.

reactions.situation: A family offers to pay to keep the old sound
reactions.response: Ren asks the engine owner what can be kept without postponing necessary repairs.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Ren looks for a second safe place to sit and stays long enough for the waiting people to settle.
